topicName: Failover Clustering Instances (FCI) and Shared Storage
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Failover Clustering Instances (FCI) and Shared Storage in Microsoft SQL Server"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"High Availability (HA) is a critical requirement for enterprise database systems. In Microsoft SQL Server, Failover Clustering Instances (FCI) provide high availability at the server instance level using shared storage and Windows Server Failover Clustering (WSFC)."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Architecture Overview"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"An FCI is installed across multiple Windows Server nodes that are part of a WSFC cluster. At any given time, only one node owns and runs the SQL Server instance. If that active node fails, the WSFC automatically fails over the SQL Server instance to one of the passive nodes."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Shared Storage: Storage Area Network (SAN), iSCSI, or SMB file shares are attached to all cluster nodes, but accessed by only one node at a time."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Virtual Network Name (VNN): Clients connect to a virtual network name and IP address, abstracting the underlying physical nodes."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Instance-Level Protection: Unlike Always On Availability Groups which protect databases, FCI protects the entire SQL Server instance including logins, jobs, and certificates."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites for FCI Deployment"},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A configured Windows Server Failover Cluster (WSFC) with at least two nodes."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Properly configured shared storage accessible via cluster disks or clustered shared volumes (CSV)."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Matching domain accounts and local administrator privileges across all cluster nodes."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Step-by-Step Installation Guide"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"To install a SQL Server Failover Cluster Instance, follow these high-level steps:"},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 1: Run the SQL Server setup program on the first cluster node and select 'Add node to a SQL Server failover cluster' or 'New SQL Server failover cluster installation'."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 2: Specify the network name and cluster resource group for the SQL Server instance."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 3: Select the shared disks to be included in the SQL Server cluster resource group."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 4: Configure the IP addresses for the SQL Server network name."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 5: Complete the installation wizard on the primary node, then run the 'Add Node' wizard on the remaining passive nodes."},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Validating the Failover Configuration"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"After installation, you should test the failover process to ensure that the shared storage and SQL Server services transition smoothly between nodes without data loss."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"-- Check current active node of the SQL Server instance\nSELECT @@SERVERNAME as ActiveNode;"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Use the Failover Cluster Manager console to manually move the SQL Server role from Node A to Node B. Verify that the application reconnects successfully through the Virtual Network Name."}]
